analysis: Integration review of the SSD prefix-cache retirement slicing (T-041, TB-007, A-001). The replayed source now includes SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices, which resolves the earlier open question. It uses filesPerSlice=16 and calls the retire closure per slice. It breaks on the first nil (refusal) and returns the accumulated totals. It unions removed, sums indexedBytesFreed and ORs externalChange. An empty batch makes exactly one ownership-checked call that returns an empty result or breaks. Both retireIndexedEntries call sites (SSDPrefixCache.swift ~1793, SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift ~33) take removalLock per slice and re-evaluate hasSafeRoot && ownsEvictionRoot. Each slice goes through the unchanged SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove, so the epoch durable-record check, non-blocking lease, no-follow status and index update are preserved. A refusal mid-batch fails closed: later files are left untouched, and the new tests (SSDOwnedEntryRetirementTests.swift ~105-151) cover that, including loss of ownership after the first slice. Only already-removed files are reported, so the index and accounting stay consistent. A refused or aborted batch delays cleanup, but expired or over-budget entries are retried on later sweeps. This can slightly delay TTL enforcement but does not extend the 30-minute window, so no fresh SEC-035 sign-off is needed. Crypto (DBK3/AES-GCM), HMAC naming, scope salt, TTL/budget values and the KEK purge are untouched. Batch atomicity is lost, so a concurrent donor or reader can interleave between slices. The existing lease and tryAcquire design tolerates this. Residual unverified: SSDCacheEpochStore.performOwnedRetirement and the callers (sweepExpiredEntries, SSDDiskBudget) were not replayed, and 23 integration source units were omitted. Caller assumptions about a partial sweep after a refusal are not shown to be broken. The documentation edits are consistent with the code. No findings.
